summary.prose: SQL table and view references resolve the way SQL compares names. One shared name rule decides equality everywhere: a double-quoted part keeps its exact case, any other part compares case-insensitively. A reference meets a definition when one name ends with the other's parts (db.app.users and app.users), several fits stay ambiguous, and a longer reference meets a shorter definition only if that definition is qualified. When a saved file adds a definition, inferred links to other definitions of the same name are checked again, and a settle re-tries only the pending references the saved files can affect.

api.name: SqlParser.parse
api.signature: parse(filePath: string, source: string, repo: string, repoId: number): ParseResult
postconditions: A table/view entity's stored name writes each double-quoted segment whose quoting matters (not all lower-case, or holding a dot or a space) in double quotes with its exact text; other segments are written as today. So ids are unchanged for definitions whose stored name does not change, and distinct definitions under the name rule ("Users" vs Users, "a.b" vs a.b) get distinct ids and are all kept. Names the grammar cannot read (brackets, escaped quotes, backticks with a dot) keep today's behaviour.
Same-file references and a view's CTE names are matched by the collision-free key, so a quoted single-segment name "a.b" never answers a qualified reference a.b.
A pending REFERENCES row's rawTo is the reference as written (quotes kept).

returns.meaning: Only the pending SQL REFERENCES rows the saved files can affect.

preconditions: Runs only when a committed file is .sql (unchanged).
postconditions: Returns a pending SQL REFERENCES row (not in scope, not awaiting an id) when its last-segment key equals the last-segment key of a table/view now defined in a committed file, or it is ambiguous and a candidate id in its meta is no longer stored, or the commit returned it to pending by name (it carries the marker the re-pend writes).
After the settle's resolution pass, the re-pend marker is cleared on every row it selected because of the marker, whether the row resolved, stayed ambiguous or no-candidate, or kept its class.

api.name: sqlByNameRows
api.signature: function sqlByNameRows(s: GraphStore, awaiting: UnresolvedRow, fromU64: bigint, toU64: bigint): UnresolvedRow[] | undefined

returns.meaning: By-name rows for the holder's written names that could mean the removed target, each carrying the re-pend marker.

postconditions: A written name of the holder is kept when it meets the target under the sqlCandidates suffix rule by the new key, OR when its folded text (today's lower-cased comparison) meets the target's folded name -- the wider of the two, so a definition stored before the change under a lossy name ("Users" stored as Users) still returns its references to pending when its file is re-read and its id changes; resolution then decides by the key. Re-pending is only a trigger to re-attempt, so the wider match never creates an edge.

A written name is skipped when it matches (by key) a table/view defined in the holder's own file: the reader resolved it there (evidence extracted), and re-pending it would create a false pending row beside the kept local edge.

dataModelChanges.entity: SQL name key (shared helper used by the reader, the resolver and the store)
dataModelChanges.details: A pure function from a written SQL name, as the grammar gives it, to its segments and its comparison key. Segments: the object_reference's identifier children (the grammar already splits at dots outside double quotes); a double-quoted segment keeps its inner text exactly, a backticked segment is unquoted and lower-cased, a bare segment is lower-cased. The equality key is the JSON encoding of the folded segment array (e.g. ["app","users"] vs ["a.b"]), so the quoted single segment "a.b" and the qualified name a.b never collide; suffix matching compares the segment arrays, and the index keys by the folded last segment. ANSI/PostgreSQL folding. Grammar limits (the installed @derekstride/tree-sitter-sql, probed 2026-11-03): it has no bracketed identifier (CREATE TABLE [Sales.Q1] parses as identifiers Sales and Q1 with the brackets as ERROR nodes, and REFERENCES [x] is skipped), no escaped double quote ("a""b" parses as "a" plus an ERROR), and a backtick identifier holding a dot (`a.b`) parses as a broken identifier plus an ERROR. This Story does not recover text the grammar loses: such names keep exactly today's behaviour (the reader reads what the grammar gives), stated as a limitation and pinned by real-parser tests so the change cannot make them worse. Supported delimiters are double quotes (any text but an escaped quote, dots included) and backticks without a dot. Lives beside the SQL reader so the store and resolver import it without loading the grammar.

dataModelChanges.entity: table/view entity name (and so its id) and pending REFERENCES rawTo
dataModelChanges.details: The entity name carries every segment boundary and the quoting that changes meaning, so distinct definitions under the name rule get distinct ids and a stored name reads back to the same key as the reference that wrote it. Each segment is written as today (its unquoted text) unless it needs quoting: a double-quoted segment needs it when its text is not all lower-case or holds a character a bare identifier cannot (a dot, a space); it is then written in double quotes with its exact text. A backticked segment never needs it (backticks fold; a backtick name with a dot is a grammar limit, see the name key). So Users and "Users" are two entities (Users, "Users"); a.b and "a.b" are two (a.b, "a.b"); users, "users" and `users` stay users. Ids are unchanged for every definition whose stored name does not change; a definition whose stored name changes (meaningful quoting added, removed or changed by an edit) gets a new id, so commitFile removes the old entity and the existing removal path returns its incoming edges to pending by name -- no new commit-boundary logic. The resolver and the store read a definition's key from its stored name with the name rule. signature stays `${kind} ${name}`. A pending row's rawTo is the reference as written (quotes kept); its id changes for quoted references on the next read of the file. Legacy rows: a definition stored before the change under a lossy name keeps resolving as today until its file is read again; when it is, the old entity's incoming edges return to pending by name through the wider folded-or-key match of sqlByNameRows, and are re-resolved by key. A holder whose own pending rows were written before the change keeps unquoted rawTo until its file is read again; repo.reindex makes the whole repository consistent at once, and is the recommended step after the update.
sqlByName and sqlByLastSegment are replaced by one map from last-segment key to table/view entities (qualified or not); sqlCandidates filters it by the suffix rule.

dataModelChanges.entity: inferred SQL REFERENCES edges on a settle that adds definitions
dataModelChanges.details: Before the settle's resolution pass, for each table/view defined in a committed file, the inbound inferred REFERENCES edges of EVERY stored table/view whose folded last segment (case-insensitive, quotes ignored) equals that definition's -- the committed definitions themselves included -- whose holder is not in a committed file are returned to pending by name (the same by-name rows sqlByNameRows writes, with the re-pend marker), then re-attempted in the same settle by key: one candidate re-resolves (inferred), several become ambiguous. Grouping by the folded last segment, and including the committed definitions, covers every case where a definition's meaning changes while its id survives: a quote-only edit, and a legacy file whose Users and "Users" were stored as one entity Users -- when re-read it keeps Users and adds "Users", and the edge an external "Users" reference had to Users is re-checked and re-resolves to "Users". The re-pend uses sqlByNameRows' rules: only the holder's names that could mean that target, never a name the holder's own file defines (resolved locally by the reader). Edges the reader resolved in its own file (evidence extracted) are never touched.

dataModelChanges.entity: re-pend marker on pending SQL REFERENCES rows
dataModelChanges.details: A meta flag set on every by-name row written by sqlByNameRows (a removed target) and by the settle's re-pend of inferred edges. Lifecycle: the next settle's sqlReferencesAwaitingCommitted selects a marked row, and after that settle's resolution pass the marker is cleared on every selected row whatever the outcome -- resolved rows leave the pending table; rows that stay ambiguous, no-candidate or unchanged in class get a metadata update that deletes the flag (a new change site beside updatePendingMetaInTxn / updateUnresolvedMetaBatch, which today only merge fields). So a marked row is retried exactly once, by the settle after the commit that marked it, and an unrelated later save does not select it again. A full index ignores and clears the flag.

The from-entity is never its own target.
Same-file references are resolved by the reader (evidence extracted) and are never re-pended by the settle.
A removed target's references return pending by name only when the reader is registered.

testLevels.purpose: The SQL name key and segment split: double-quoted exact, bare/backtick/bracket folded, dots inside quotes kept, unbalanced quotes degrade to one folded segment; the suffix rule.

The reader keeps raw names in signature and rawTo, matches same-file references and CTE names by key, and referencesIn returns names as written. Existing reader assertions that encode today's conflation are updated, not kept: in src/indexer/parser/__tests__/sql.test.ts the unquoted `orders` no longer links to CREATE TABLE "Orders" (it becomes a pending reference), FROM Totals is a reference when the CTE is WITH "Totals", and pending names keep their delimiters ("Sales", app."Ledger"); positive counterparts are added (FROM "Orders" links, FROM "Totals" is the CTE). A quoted dotted identifier must not answer a qualified reference. Same-file regressions hold both members of each collision pair (Users / "Users", a.b / "a.b") with a reference to each, and assert two entities with distinct ids and each reference linked to its own. Grammar-limit regressions with the real parser: the entities and references produced for [Sales.Q1], "a""b" and `a.b` (definitions, a view's FROM, REFERENCES, referencesIn) are the same before and after the change.

Over a temporary store with real .sql files and the cross-file resolver: 2-/3-part suffix resolution, the qualified-vs-unqualified rule, quoted vs unquoted, ambiguity kept; a settle that adds a same-named definition makes an inferred edge ambiguous and leaves other names alone; a settle re-attempts only rows the saved files can affect (unrelated pending rows untouched, an ambiguous row whose candidate was removed re-resolves). The selection is observed directly (the rows sqlReferencesAwaitingCommitted returns), not inferred from outcomes; a two-settle sequence proves a re-pended row's marker is consumed by the first settle and an unrelated later save does not retry it. Update regressions: a quote-only edit (Users -> "Users") and a segment-boundary edit (a.b -> "a.b") of a definition return another file's inferred edge to pending. Upgrade regression: a store written with today's reader (lossy names), then only the definition file re-read with the new reader, keeps the other file's reference linked to the definition. Mixed-ownership regression: a holder with one locally resolved and one inferred reference, then a same-last-segment definition added, creates no pending row for the local name. Legacy-collision regression: a store written with today's reader from one file declaring both Users and "Users", then only that file re-read with the new reader, leaves an unchanged external "Users" reference linked to the "Users" entity.

migration.stateBefore: SQL names are unquoted and compared lower-cased everywhere, qualified references meet only identical names, inferred edges are never re-checked, and any .sql save re-attempts every pending SQL reference (s1 bundles 1-4).
migration.stateAfter: One name key with ANSI quoting decides equality in the reader, resolver and store; qualified names meet by segment suffix; a settle that adds definitions re-checks same-named inferred edges; a settle re-attempts only rows its files can affect.

migrationSteps.action: Ship the change; no schema or codec change.

Definitions whose quoting does not change meaning keep their names and ids; definitions with meaningful quoting (rare) get a quoted name and a new id when their file is read again, their old rows removed by the normal commit; quoted references' pending rows get new ids the same way.

Run repo.reindex once after the update so every definition and reference is read under the new rule at the same time (recommended). Without it the change is still safe: when a definition file is read again, the settle re-checks the inferred incoming edges of every same-named definition (its own included), and a removed one's edges return to pending through the wider folded-or-key match; a holder written before the change compares as unquoted, today's behaviour, until its file is read again.

migration.backwardCompat: No API, IPC or storage format change. Visible differences: more resolved SQL references (qualified names), quoted names no longer conflated, stale inferred edges become ambiguous when a second definition appears.

alternativesConsidered.name: One SQL name key + suffix matching + re-pend on a new candidate + targeted settle
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: A shared name key (ANSI quoting) used by the reader, the resolver and the store; qualified names meet by segment suffix; a new definition returns same-named inferred edges to pending; a settle re-attempts only rows the saved files can affect.
alternativesConsidered.approach: A shared SQL name module defines the comparison key: names split into segments at dots outside quotes; a double-quoted segment keeps its exact text, any other segment (bare, backticked, bracketed) is lower-cased (ANSI / PostgreSQL folding). The reader keeps the raw declared name in each table/view entity's signature and in each pending row's rawTo, and matches same-file references and CTE names by key. The resolver indexes definitions by the key of their last segment and accepts a candidate whose segments match the reference's from the end over the shorter length, where a reference longer than the definition needs the definition to be qualified (db.app.users meets app.users; audit.users does not meet a bare users); several candidates stay ambiguous. The store's removal re-pend compares by key too. When a settle commits definitions, inferred REFERENCES edges into other definitions with the same last-segment key are returned to pending by name (the removal path's by-name rows) and re-attempted in the same settle, so a second candidate makes them ambiguous. The settle re-attempts only pending SQL rows whose last-segment key matches a definition in a committed file, ambiguous rows whose candidates include an entity no longer stored, and rows the commit returned to pending.
pros: Each gap fixed with one consistent name rule used everywhere SQL names are compared
Settle cost proportional to the names the saved files touch
cons: Quoting folds by ANSI/PostgreSQL rules; MySQL/SQL Server dialects that treat quoted identifiers case-insensitively are approximated
Entities of quoted objects get a signature with quotes; ids unchanged (names stay unquoted)
L1 covers SQL only; CALLS keeps its behaviour

alternativesConsidered.name: Fix L4 and L3 only; leave edges and settle as they are
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Name key and suffix matching; no re-check of inferred edges and no narrower settle.
alternativesConsidered.approach: The name key and suffix matching from a1, without the re-pend of inferred edges on a new candidate and without narrowing the settle re-scan.
cons: Leaves L1 (stale inferred edge) and L2 (whole-repository re-scan per .sql save) unfixed, contrary to the ISSUE's fix intent

alternativesConsidered.name: Store canonical keys in new entity and row fields
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Add a nameKey field to table/view entities and pending rows instead of keeping raw names in signature and rawTo.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Extend the Entity and UnresolvedRelation records with a stored key computed at read time; the resolver and store compare keys without re-deriving them.
pros: No re-parsing of raw names at resolution time
cons: A storage format change (codec fields) for every table/view and pending row, with a migration, for a value a pure function derives from the raw name in microseconds
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Same outcome as a1 with a storage migration it does not need.

citations.quotedText: function resolveSqlReference(row: UnresolvedRelation, index: EntityIndex): ResolveIntent {
function sqlByNameRows(s: GraphStore, awaiting: UnresolvedRow, fromU64: bigint, toU64: bigint): UnresolvedRow[] | undefined {
